text: Ministry launches comprehensive review of fuel storage and distribution network

Under its Decision No. 3055, dated November 17, 2026, the Ministry of Industry and Trade (MoIT) has approved a plan for the revision of the National Petroleum and Gas Storage and Supply Infrastructure Plan for the 2021-2030 period, with a vision to 2050, according to the Government's online newspaper (chinhphu.vn).

The revision aims to align the plan with the country's economic development requirements in the new context and ensure consistency with the National Energy Storage Strategy to 2030, with a vision to 2045.

A key task of the review is to comprehensively assess the implementation of the existing plan, including the relevance of its guiding principles, objectives, targets, development orientations, and infrastructure development schemes.
The adjustment will also update the names, boundaries, and administrative jurisdictions of localities following recent administrative restructuring.
Place names, project locations, and addresses will be standardized, while spatial planning arrangements for infrastructure development will be reviewed.
In addition, the revised plan will update forecasts for fuel and gas supply, demand, and storage requirements across different regions.

Based on the review findings, demand projections, and national energy security requirements, authorities will propose adjustments to infrastructure development plans and project portfolios, specifying locations, scales, capacities, implementation timelines, investment phases, and connectivity solutions.
The review will also determine land-use requirements, marine space allocation, and investment needs, while proposing mechanisms to mobilize resources and organize implementation.
Results from the strategic environmental assessment will be used to compare, select, and finalize the adjusted development scenario.
Notably, the planning revision will be cross-checked against the revised National Energy Master Plan for 2021-2030, with a vision to 2050, as well as regional, provincial, and other related plans.
Overlapping, conflicting, or inconsistent provisions will be identified and addressed to ensure coherence and alignment across planning frameworks.
At the same time, planning diagrams and databases will be updated and standardized to reflect the revised plan.
Under the implementation schedule, the revised planning dossier is expected to be completed and submitted to the MoIT for review and approval in the third quarter of 2027.
